correctness.rationale: Starting from g+=(0,g2-c*g1/a), GSL selection imposes |g2/g1|<=sqrt(b/a)=s. The exact worst opposite-sign ratio yields q^2+2qs<=1 (q=|c|/a). For fixed q²=u and s²=y the normalized spectral spread delta²=[(1-y)²+4u]/(1+y)² is minimized over unsafe region. Along boundary y=(1-u)²/(4u), stationarity gives 3u²-8u+1=0, u*=(4-sqrt13)/3, delta_*²=(97-26sqrt13)/27. For larger q range the minimal spread >=1/8>delta_*², so the threshold is global. Strict unsafe matrices for every larger kappa arise increasing s at fixed q*. Independent exact rational check for A=[[1,1/2],[1/2,1]], g=(1,-9/10): g+=(0,-7/5), norm squared factor 196/181>1 while objective decreases 1/2. Boundary equality includes GSL ties. Verification script algebra inspected; finite checks are not the proof.

value.rationale: Gradient norm is a standard practical stationarity stopping diagnostic, while a GSL update is chosen to maximize objective decrease. A sharp matrix-condition boundary for whether this distinct diagnostic can worsen has direct structural and algorithmic meaning. The explicit fixed-matrix cone criterion and a unique-choice counterexample show exactly why objective descent does not guarantee gradient-norm descent. Not merely a normalization of the GSL definition.
